gap_severity_basis: The lack of standardized Green ICT indicators limits consistent measurement of environmental performance.
barrier_severity_basis: Measurement and disclosure limitations create a barrier to consistent assessment across operators.
environmental_impact_basis: Standardized measurement can support identification of environmental improvement opportunities.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Standardized KPIs, baselines, and reporting procedures are generally feasible to implement.

gap_severity_basis: Insufficient operator-level GHG and e-waste information limits assessment of environmental performance.
barrier_severity_basis: Measurement, disclosure, and comparability limitations make GHG and e-waste management difficult to monitor.
environmental_impact_basis: Improved GHG and e-waste data can support emissions reduction, recycling, and waste-management improvements.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Standardized disclosure and tracking procedures are generally feasible to establish.

gap_severity_basis: Rising energy consumption and emissions indicate a significant need for improved network energy efficiency and energy-demand management.
barrier_severity_basis: Energy use and emissions management require operational improvements and continued monitoring.
environmental_impact_basis: Improved network energy efficiency can substantially reduce energy consumption and associated emissions.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Energy-efficiency measures are generally feasible but may require operational and technical changes.

gap_severity_basis: Physical renewable-energy adoption remains limited or uneven across network sites.
barrier_severity_basis: Renewable deployment can face technical, infrastructure, and implementation barriers.
environmental_impact_basis: Solar and hybrid renewable-energy systems can substantially reduce dependence on higher-emission energy sources.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Implementation is technically feasible where site conditions permit but may require investment.

gap_severity_basis: Unresolved renewable-energy procurement mechanisms can directly constrain implementation.
barrier_severity_basis: Procurement and regulatory barriers can significantly restrict renewable-energy access.
environmental_impact_basis: Greater renewable-energy procurement can substantially increase renewable electricity use and support decarbonization.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Implementation depends partly on regulatory, contractual, and procurement mechanisms.

gap_severity_basis: Insufficient quantitative evidence limits assessment of infrastructure-sharing arrangements and their resource-efficiency benefits.
barrier_severity_basis: Limited disclosure and coordination create barriers to measuring infrastructure-sharing opportunities.
environmental_impact_basis: Effective infrastructure sharing can improve resource efficiency and reduce unnecessary infrastructure duplication.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Standardized reporting is feasible, although implementation requires coordination among operators and stakeholders.

gap_severity_basis: Organizational responsibilities and monitoring arrangements require clearer definition to support implementation of Green ICT measures.
barrier_severity_basis: Weak coordination, monitoring, and accountability can limit implementation.
environmental_impact_basis: Improved organizational implementation can support more consistent application of Green ICT measures.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Clear responsibilities, monitoring procedures, and coordination mechanisms are generally feasible to establish.

gap_severity_basis: Several Green ICT requirements require clearer quantitative targets, timelines, and verification mechanisms for measurable assessment.
barrier_severity_basis: Limited policy measurability can make implementation and verification difficult.
environmental_impact_basis: Quantitative targets and verification can improve environmental accountability and monitoring.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Implementation is feasible but requires regulatory coordination, monitoring, and verification mechanisms.
